AIYANA [SURNAME]
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [GITHUB / PORTFOLIO]

PROFESSIONAL PROFILE
Early-career web developer with hands-on frontend experience from a student hackathon project and experience supporting first-year web development students as a teaching assistant. Interested in junior frontend and full-stack opportunities. Completed introductory online learning in GraphQL; has not yet used GraphQL in a project.

TECHNICAL EXPERIENCE
Student Hackathon Project — Transit Delay Notifier | 2024
- Worked in a three-person team to build a transit delay notifier in 24 hours.
- Developed the frontend for the project.
- The team placed second in the student hackathon.

TEACHING EXPERIENCE
Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Spring 2025
- Supported approximately 30 students during one semester of first-year web development labs.

VOLUNTEER EXPERIENCE
Social Media Volunteer, Sea Swimming Club
- Run social media for a sea swimming club.

ADDITIONAL LEARNING
GraphQL — Free online course; completed introductory learning. Not yet used in a project.

AREAS OF INTEREST
Frontend development | Full-stack development

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is concise, honest, and easy to scan. The project, hackathon result, team size, time limit, teaching-assistant experience, and GraphQL learning are clearly stated. However, it is too sparse for a technical CV: the hackathon section does not identify any technologies, implementation details, functionality delivered, or measurable contribution beyond saying that the candidate developed the frontend. The profile also foregrounds limitations, especially “has not yet used GraphQL in a project,” rather than presenting the strongest evidence first. The contact placeholders make the document unsuitable for submission in its current form.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The single-column section structure and standard headings should parse well. However, ATS matching for this role will be weak because the CV contains none of the job's supported technical keywords such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, SQL, automated testing, Git, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, authentication, or OWASP Top 10. These must not be added without evidence, but the CV should describe the actual technologies and development practices used in the hackathon if they are known and supportable. “Technical Experience” currently contains almost no technical terminology. Replace all bracketed contact fields with real details before submission, and include a real GitHub, portfolio, or project URL only if one exists. Estimated AI screening probability for this specific role: low, primarily because the CV does not demonstrate the mandatory experience level or core stack.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is limited. The CV supports early-career frontend potential, collaborative delivery under time pressure, student support, and interest in frontend/full-stack development. The second-place hackathon result and teaching-assistant experience may appeal to a low-ego, mentoring-oriented team. However, the candidate's material does not show the role's required 2+ years of professional React and TypeScript experience, backend services in Node.js, SQL databases, automated unit or end-to-end testing, Git workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, web security, authentication, OWASP Top 10, or fluent English. It also does not show any of the listed nice-to-have experience. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that rewriting can solve. The CV should therefore present the existing frontend project and teaching experience accurately without implying full-stack, healthcare, security, or production experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES
1. In the header, replace “AIYANA [SURNAME]”, “[EMAIL]”, “[PHONE]”, “[LINKEDIN]”, and “[GITHUB / PORTFOLIO]” with the candidate’s actual name and contact details before submitting. Remove any unused placeholder field rather than leaving brackets in the final CV.
2. In the “Student Hackathon Project — Transit Delay Notifier” entry, expand the existing bullets using only verified facts from the project. State what frontend functionality the candidate personally implemented and what the notifier allowed users to do, if those details are available. Do not add React, TypeScript, APIs, testing, Git, or other tools unless they were actually used.
3. In the same project entry, change the generic bullet “Developed the frontend for the project” into a more specific contribution statement based on the candidate’s real work. For example, use wording such as “Built the frontend interface for a transit delay notifier as part of a three-person team during a 24-hour hackathon” if that accurately reflects the work. Keep the second-place result prominent.

MINOR / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
4. In “PROFESSIONAL PROFILE,” remove the sentence “has not yet used GraphQL in a project.” It is truthful but unnecessarily frames the candidate around a limitation in the opening section. Keep the factual course entry in “ADDITIONAL LEARNING,” where it is sufficient to write “Completed an introductory GraphQL online course.”
5. In “PROFESSIONAL PROFILE,” replace “Interested in junior frontend and full-stack opportunities” with a more evidence-led statement focused on the demonstrated profile, such as “Early-career web developer with frontend project experience, collaborative hackathon delivery, and experience supporting first-year web development students.” Do not describe the candidate as a full-stack engineer or claim backend capability.
6. In “TEACHING EXPERIENCE,” make the existing contribution more informative without overstating it. For example, change the bullet to “Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development labs by helping them work through coursework and practical exercises,” but retain only the activities the candidate actually performed.
7. In “VOLUNTEER EXPERIENCE,” change “Run social media for a sea swimming club” to a consistent past- or present-tense CV bullet, such as “Manage social media for a sea swimming club.” Add platforms, content types, posting frequency, audience growth, or engagement figures only if the candidate can verify them.
8. Rename “TECHNICAL EXPERIENCE” to “PROJECT EXPERIENCE” unless the candidate can substantiate additional technical experience. Rename “ADDITIONAL LEARNING” to “COURSES & ADDITIONAL LEARNING” only if it will contain further factual learning entries; otherwise the current heading is acceptable.
critique.critical_issues: The document contains unresolved submission placeholders in the name and contact section, which must be replaced before use. It does not contain apparent hallucinated skills or experience: the GraphQL limitation is explicitly disclosed, and the hackathon, teaching-assistant, and volunteer claims are consistent with the candidate’s notes. The absence of the job’s technical requirements is a candidate-profile gap, not a hallucination or a defect to conceal through unsupported keyword insertion.

Experience writing backend services in Node.js and working with SQL databases

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clean, concise, and easy to scan. It accurately presents the candidate's limited but relevant experience without overstating GraphQL or backend capability. The strongest evidence is the second-place hackathon result, the three-person team context, the 24-hour delivery constraint, and support provided to approximately 30 students. However, the document is too sparse for a technical engineering application: it contains no contact details, portfolio/GitHub links, education information, named technologies, measurable teaching outcomes, or detail about the frontend work performed. The profile is professional but generic, and the separate Areas of Interest section does not compensate for the lack of technical evidence.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The section headings and simple formatting should parse reliably in most ATS systems. There are no tables, columns, graphics, icons, or unusual formatting. However, ATS screening probability for this specific role is low because the CV does not contain the core searchable terms React, TypeScript, Node.js, SQL, automated testing, unit testing, end-to-end testing, Git, authentication, OWASP, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, or accessibility. These omissions appear to reflect unsupported or undocumented experience rather than merely poor keyword usage, so the terms must not be added without factual evidence. The document also lacks standard contact fields and a portfolio/GitHub URL, which reduces recruiter usability and the chance of validating the project.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is weak for the advertised Full-Stack Engineer role. The CV supports early-career frontend exposure, collaborative delivery, student mentoring, and interest in frontend/full-stack development. It does not demonstrate the required 2+ years of professional React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend services, SQL databases, automated unit and end-to-end testing, Git workflows, web security fundamentals, or the healthcare/privacy context. The candidate notes also state that there is no backend job experience and that GraphQL has not been used in a project. The hackathon and teaching experience provide some positive evidence for teamwork, delivery under time pressure, and mentoring, but they do not establish the role's core engineering requirements. No evidence is provided for the nice-to-have qualifications.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the document header, add the candidate's current professional contact details: email address, phone number, and relevant LinkedIn, GitHub, portfolio, or live-project links where those genuinely exist. Do not add placeholder links.
2. In the Professional Profile section, replace the generic opening with a more evidence-based summary such as: "Early-career web developer with frontend delivery experience from a three-person, 24-hour student hackathon project that placed second, plus one semester supporting approximately 30 first-year web development students." This makes the strongest verified evidence immediately visible without implying professional full-stack experience.
3. In the Transit Delay Notifier project entry, add factual implementation detail about the frontend work—such as the actual framework, language, UI features, collaboration tools, testing, or deployment method—only where it is known and supported by the candidate's records. Do not add React, TypeScript, Git, testing, accessibility, or other job keywords unless they were genuinely used.
4. In the Teaching Experience section, expand the bullet with the actual support activities performed, if documented—for example, whether the candidate explained concepts, debugged student code, reviewed exercises, or helped students use development tools. This would make the mentoring and communication evidence more relevant to the role without inventing responsibilities.
5. In the Project Experience section, add a project link or repository link for the Transit Delay Notifier if one exists and is presentable. A verifiable project is particularly important because the CV currently provides no way to assess the candidate's frontend work.

MINOR IMPROVEMENTS
6. Rename "Areas of Interest" to "Technical Focus" only if the section continues to describe genuine interests, and retain the distinction between interest and experience. For example: "Frontend development | Full-stack development interest." This avoids making full-stack development appear to be an established competency.
7. In the Additional Learning section, retain the qualification that GraphQL was introductory and not used in a project, but format it as "GraphQL — Introductory online course" for quicker scanning. Do not list GraphQL as professional project experience.
8. Standardize the experience formatting by adding an organization or project context wherever available, using consistent date formatting across all entries. Do not invent an institution or employer name if it was not supplied.
